newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria c.bank seeks insolvency for eight banks.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria c.bank seeks insolvency for eight banks.

text.p: Bulgaria's central bank, moving to clean up its crumbling banking system at the start of an IMF mission, said on Thursday it had begun bankruptcy proceedings for eight of nine banks placed in receivership in September.
"The BNB Board decided to seek bankruptcy for eight banks on the basis of their insolvency," the Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) said in a statement.

The BNB also cut its central interest rate to 180 percent from 240 percent. The rate was raised to an all-time high of 300 percent on September 23, when the bank placed the nine banks in receivership, in a bid to attract money back into the banking system.

The BNB has been under heavy pressure from the Socialist government to ease credit because high rates are stifling what little economic activity remains. Domestic debt has doubled since the start of the year.
Economy Minister Roumen Gechev said recently it was impossible to plan a 1997 budget under current interest rates.
The central bank also said it was closing 22 financial brokerage houses for violation of BNB rules.

Brokerage houses frequently attract BNB criticism for participating directly in the foreign exchange market instead of through the banks and artificially weakening the lev. The bank pledged last week to close the worst offenders.

The cleanup measures coincide with the visit of an International Monetary Fund mission to Sofia to discuss terms for release of a $115 million credit, vital if the small Balkan country is to avoid default on its foreign debt next year.
The IMF postponed the credit until Bulgaria closed 64 loss-making state enterprises and stabilised its financial system.

Slack lending controls, siphoning of funds abroad and lack of structural reform since the end of communist rule in 1989 have all contributed to the collapse of the banking system. The country has 47 banks for a population of 8.4 million.
The BNB named the eight insolvent banks as Balkanbank, Businessbank, Dobrudhza Bank, Mollov Bank, Slavyani Bank, Economic Bank, Trade and Savings Bank and Yambol Bank.
Balkanbank, Economic Bank and Yambol Bank are state-owned, the rest are private.
The eight banks, plus private Elitbank, were placed in receivership on September 23 with delayed settlement payments totalling 11.4 billion levs ($47.5 million).
The BNB began insolvency proceedings against five other banks in June but courts have so far delayed ruling on those cases.
The BNB said it would continue to discuss the financial status of Elitbank, which has the least negative capital to risk assets ratio.
